core_job: For people who drive the same roads every week: get me there and warn me about what is on this road, my own hazards and official ones, in the order I will meet them. The flow is search, then Route check, then turn-by-turn with the ahead rail, then arrival, with a one-time ETA share. Routing is OSRM, search is Nominatim, the map is flutter_map with CARTO/OSM tiles. Most of this already works. It needs the false and overlapping parts removed (sign-in, radio, emergency dialler, AI labels, demo code) and its own identity.
signature: Road Notes: private hazard notes stored on the phone. Mark a spot and choose Remember, and iMaps warns you every time you approach it in the same direction, while navigating (ahead rail plus banner) or in free drive (400 m ahead, heading within ±45°, speed over 15 km/h). A note can be conditional: always, a weekday time window, or after rain (Open-Meteo past_hours precipitation at that spot; keyless; multi-location call curl-verified 200 on 2026-10-12; if the rain data cannot be fetched, the note still warns). Route check shows, for each route, the notes that will be active when you reach them plus NWS, USGS and GDACS alerts along the way, and says how many points were really checked: 2 of 19 NWS points returned HTTP 500 in my probe. Competitor basis: App Store descriptions read through the iTunes Search API, not hands-on testing. Waze shares reports publicly. Apple Maps has personal notes on places but its description mentions no approach warnings. Route-weather apps (Weather on the Way, Drive Weather, Highway Weather) already exist, so route weather is deliberately not the headline.
